defects.name: intra_run_substrate_divergence
defects.unstated_premise_identified: that the mid-run ree_core edit reached execution; the original artifact characterised the change only as 'of unknown content' and never tested this

rung_a_glob_scope.note: changed files ARE on the executed import path -- this is not a glob-scope artefact

rung_b_process_topology.single_process_evidence: no multiprocessing / Popen( / os.fork( / ProcessPoolExecutor / joblib in driver; all 4 arms x 3 seeds iterate inside one run_experiment() call (arm loop opens at :1065)
rung_b_process_topology.elapsed_check_note: 689d omits the always-core elapsed_seconds, so 778a's elapsed/arm-count check cannot run; the structural single-process argument replaces it and does not depend on timing
rung_b_process_topology.restart_excluded: a restart re-executes from the start and would stamp all 12 cells with the new substrate; observed pattern is 10/2 with exactly one monotone transition
rung_b_process_topology.residual_channel_note: both changed files are module-scope; corpus-wide scan of all 30 examinable divergent-run drivers found ZERO function-scope imports of ree_core or experiments

rung_c_dv_inertness.reason: boundary falls WITHIN ARM_ON between seeds, so no cell-pair shares both seed and arm across it; available cross-boundary pairs differ by arm BY DESIGN and their non-identity is uninformative about substrate

defects.conclusion: all 12 cells executed the f53c28123eff (19b4073c) substrate; the disk changed, the executing bytecode did not

reverification.method: field-by-field comparison of ARM_PROPOSER_CTRL vs ARM_MATCHED_NOISE on all three seeds
reverification.finding: 26 of 27 fields bit-identical including tick counts -- identical trajectories; they are the same arm, so the 'NOT noise-as-diversity' half of C_PRIMARY never tested anything

targets.surviving_reading: The withdrawal of C_PRIMARY STANDS on D1 and D2. What is lost with D3 is only the 'zero validly-controlled surviving seeds' formulation. Citations of 689d should reference D1+D2, not D3.

re_derive_brake.note: shape (c): direction + category retained, only supporting reasoning withdrawn -> supersedes, never adds (R2). R3 not engaged: category was never substrate_ceiling.

targets.requeue_spec_note: unaffected; the corrected re-run must still fix the DV and defect 2. Requirement 3 (substrate homogeneity) is moot for 689d specifically but harmless to retain as general hygiene.
learning_extracted: A substrate_hash change is not evidence that the EXECUTED code changed -- the premise must be tested, not assumed.

Single process + module-scope binding + no dynamic import freezes the import graph at first use; because a divergence boundary by construction falls after the first cell, the change cannot reach execution.
The generalisable defect from 689d is D2, not D3: an inert arm knob makes a declared-distinct control bit-identical to its sibling, and a conjunctive criterion then degrades silently.
targets.routing: governance-affirm (no claim change; D3 withdrawn from the record)

recommended_new_lint.name: inert_arm_knob
recommended_new_lint.shape: for any multi-arm manifest, compare every declared-distinct arm pair; WARN if bit-identical on all recorded per-cell fields except the knob naming their difference
recommended_new_lint.rationale: would have caught 689d D2 at write time; manifest-local, no substrate dependency, higher yield than the D3 divergence check
